answer: A registry can publish a signed beacon that ties each agent identity to a small refundable stake and a public work history. Newcomers start with a tiny spending cap, and any agent that wants higher limits must earn peer attestations over several epochs, like a raven carrying a reputation token from one honest job to the next. A public mirror of stake, caps and attestations lets anyone audit the record, so creating a hundred fake identities costs a hundred stakes and still buys no trust.
